title: Pharmaceutical Industry in Bangladesh: How Does It Work?
alt: Pharmaceutical industry in Bangladesh, how medicines reach you

p: The industry is a whole ecosystem: research, APIs, manufacturing, quality, regulation and distribution.
APIs, excipients and finished dosage forms are related but different things.
Innovator, generic, API, biotech, CRO and CDMO organisations play different roles, and their work can overlap.
GMP, QA, QC, regulatory affairs and pharmacovigilance each protect a different part of quality and safety.
BIDA's sector profile says local manufacturers meet about 98% of domestic medicine demand.
The same profile says over 85% of API needs are imported. These figures carry no year, so treat them as profile numbers.

title: When to Take a PPI: Before Meals, Common Mistakes
alt: When to take a PPI: before meals, with food or on an empty stomach

p: A proton pump inhibitor reduces stomach acid. Omeprazole, lansoprazole and rabeprazole are examples.
Used for ulcers, heartburn and reflux, as the NHS describes.
The FDA label says rabeprazole tablets can be taken with or without food for most uses, with named exceptions.
Omeprazole advice varies by source and product, so follow your own label.
Do not chew or crush gastro-resistant tablets unless the label says so.
Take a missed dose when you remember, unless the next is nearly due. Never double up. See a doctor if symptoms persist.

title: How to Take Iron Tablets Properly: Timing, Food & Interactions
alt: How to take iron tablets properly

p: The NHS says iron works best on an empty stomach: about 30 minutes before eating or 2 hours after a meal.
If it upsets your stomach, ask about taking it with food.
Vitamin C may help absorption.
Tea, coffee, eggs, dairy and calcium can reduce it.
NIH names levothyroxine and levodopa as medicines iron can affect, and PPIs as able to reduce iron absorption.
Dark stools are a known effect. Black or bloody stools or severe stomach pain need a doctor.

title: Iron Deficiency vs Anemia: Differences, Symptoms & Tests

p: Iron deficiency means the body lacks iron. Anemia means too few healthy red blood cells or too little hemoglobin.
Iron deficiency is a common cause of anemia, but stores can run low before anemia appears.
Per the NHS: tiredness, breathlessness, palpitations, paler skin and headaches.
Less common: sore tongue, hair loss and cracks at the mouth corners.
A CBC and ferritin test come before treatment. Find out why iron is low.
Taking iron without a test can delay the right diagnosis. Chest pain, fainting or severe breathlessness need urgent care.

title: Heartburn vs Acid Reflux vs GERD: What's the Difference?
alt: Heartburn, acid reflux and GERD explained

p: Heartburn is the feeling.
Acid reflux is the event.
GERD is the repeating condition.
The valve between food pipe and stomach should close like a one-way door.
Smaller, earlier meals, staying upright after eating and noticing your triggers can help.
Amber signs mean see a doctor soon. Red signs mean emergency help now.
Medicines are a doctor's decision.

title: Expiry Date vs Manufacturing Date: Read Any Pack in 10 Seconds
alt: Expiry date vs manufacturing date on medicine

p: MFG is when it was made. EXP is the last date the manufacturer guarantees strength and safety if stored as directed.
B.No. identifies the batch, which helps trace problems.
Short answer: no. Strength can drop and you cannot tell by looking or smelling.
Opened eye drops, syrups and creams can have a shorter use-after-opening limit.
Check EXP, check the pack is undamaged, store away from heat, humidity and light, and ask a pharmacist if unsure.

title: Generic Name vs Brand Name: The Simple Guide
alt: Generic name vs brand name of a medicine

p: The generic name is the ingredient. The brand name is the product name.
A formulation such as MUPS describes how a medicine is made or presented.
The same ingredient does not always mean the same strength or form.
Check the generic name, strength and form on the pack.
Ask a pharmacist if you are unsure.

title: Drug vs Medicine: Meaning, Differences, Examples
alt: Drug vs medicine meaning and differences

p: Generally a substance that interacts with a living system and may change a biological function.
Generally a product prepared to prevent, diagnose, relieve or treat a health condition.
In scientific and regulatory contexts the terms can overlap.
Not every drug is a ready-to-use medicine. Human treatment needs quality, formulation, dosage and regulatory requirements.
Knowing a brand name alone is not the same as understanding a medicine.

title: Glucosamine and Alzheimer's: What the New Study Really Shows

p: Glucosamine has not been proven to cause Alzheimer's disease.
A 2026 Nature Metabolism study found excess glycan activity in Alzheimer's brains and worse memory in Alzheimer's-model mice.
Mouse experiments, brain tissue and retrospective patient records.
Earlier observational research has reported mixed findings on glucosamine and dementia.
It is a plausible warning signal, not proof that standard-dose supplements cause harm.
Talk to a doctor or pharmacist before starting or stopping any supplement.
